_notes: Fit of a real cable clamped to a gripper that follows a recorded TCP trajectory, against camera masks.
The recordings are not in this repository; pass their directory with --recordings. Each holds the TCP drive, the camera, and one cable mask per observation.
Cable: 0.5 m in total, 0.174 kg (0.348 kg/m), about 16 mm diameter. The gripper holds the first 0.02 m; the grasp point is at the TCP.
discretization: 10 capsules model the free 0.48 m; one more capsule inside the gripper ends at the grasp point and is the kinematic clamp (clamp 'stub').
rest_shape: one (x, y) bend pair per joint, as arc displacement [m] at the cable end, bounded by max_angle_rad times the joint's lever.
The observation is the chamfer score of the projected free cable against the mask, in cable lengths on screen. Its reference is 0.
scale: expected chamfer score of a good fit [cable lengths on screen]. An estimate; the score of a perfect fit is not zero, because distances are to the cable axis.
Units: rigidities are per length (EI, EA, GA, GJ), dampings per length; the backend divides by the segment length.
Bend damping, stretch, shear and twist are not fitted and stay fixed.
rank_tolerance: alternating rest bends near the free end change the silhouette little; their singular values are about 6e-4 of the largest. 1e-4 keeps them in the search.
Stretch and shear rigidity are stiff enough that the cable does not stretch significantly.
fps: the simulation frame rate. Each observation is taken at the solver step nearest to its camera time stamp.
settle_frames: the cable is within 1 mm of rest after at most about 40 frames over the EI bounds; 120 frames (2 s) leave a margin.
